memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses, "These are the regulations for any diseased person at the time of their ceremonial cleansing, when they are brought to the priest." - Lev 14:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Stop and take in what has just happened. God has given a law for restoration.

Think of the person this was written for. They had been sent outside the camp. They had torn their clothes and cried "unclean" so people would keep away. They had lost their family table, their neighbours, their place in worship. Everything.

And before any of them was healed, God had already written down how to bring them home.

That is the kind of God we have. He does not wait to see whether anyone will recover before making a plan for their return. The way back was prepared in advance, written into the law, waiting.

We meet this again in the New Testament, more wonderfully still. He chose us in him before the creation of the world (Eph 1:4). Christ was the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world. The road home was built before we ever wandered off it.

If you have been away — from God, from His people, from the person you once were — hear this. God has not been caught off guard by your absence, scrambling to work out what to do with you. The way back already exists. It has your name on it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you assumed God has no plan for restoring you?
2. What does it mean that God prepared the way home before you needed it?
3. Who do you know who needs to hear that a way back exists?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that before I ever wandered, You had already made a way home. Help me to trust that Your heart towards me is restoration, not rejection. Amen.
